note: What `waf.mjs consent` asks Azure besides the closed az vectors of az-read.json: two Resource Graph reads through the fixed template (a POST of a query in a request body, never an argument), and the role table used to judge the identity. The principal id is a validated GUID inserted into the query text of CONSENT-ROLES only; the management group or subscription list goes in the request body. Output of these reads goes to the user's screen (sanitized) and to consent.json as counts, GUIDs and role names; it is never evidence. Not verified: the shape of these answers in a real tenant, and whether authorizationresources lists role assignments inherited from a management group or granted through a group the principal belongs to (it filters by the principal id only, so a group-based assignment is NOT seen: that case is reported as unverifiable, never as read-only). Manual tests M-0 and M-3.

checks.purpose: The subscriptions under the chosen scope as resourcecontainers lists them, to compare with az account list.
checks.query: resourcecontainers | where type =~ 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions' | project id, subscriptionId, displayName=tostring(properties.displayName)

checks.purpose: The role assignments whose principal is the signed-in identity.
checks.query: authorizationresources | where type =~ 'microsoft.authorization/roleassignments' | where tostring(properties.principalId) =~ '{principalId}' | project id, roleDefinitionId=tostring(properties.roleDefinitionId), scope=tostring(properties.scope)
